parts.label: (a)
parts.text:
A neuromuscular junction allows the transmission of an action potential from a motor neurone to a striated muscle fibre, causing it to contract.

Fig. 9.1 is a graph of an action potential in a motor neurone.

{{figure:figure_9_1.webp}}

Fig. 9.1

Fig. 9.2 is a graph of an action potential in a striated muscle fibre.

{{figure:figure_9_2.webp}}

Fig. 9.2

With reference to Fig. 9.1 and Fig. 9.2, describe the differences between the action potential in a motor neurone and the action potential in a striated muscle fibre.

parts.label: (b)(i)
parts.stem:
There are three phases in the contraction of a striated muscle: latent phase, contraction phase and relaxation phase.

The tension in a muscle represents the degree of contraction of its fibres.

Fig. 9.3 is a graph of the tension in a striated muscle during the three phases of contraction.

{{figure:figure_9_3.webp}}

Fig. 9.3
parts.text: With reference to Fig. 9.3, explain what is happening in the striated muscle fibre during the latent phase.

parts.label: (b)(ii)
parts.text: Suggest why the relaxation phase shows a gradual decrease in muscle tension.
